qa_rejections_7d.notes: Clean hoist-camera footage with a swimmer swinging over the wake, but it is the seventh moving-fishing-boat hoist in two days (20-27, 20-28, 20-29, 20-30, 21-04, 21-05) and its title and hook nearly repeat 20-30. Fails item 13 (interchangeable).

Third Saturn V liftoff in this batch (21-02 Apollo 11 engines, 21-06 Apollo 4) and the cloud/sound barrier lines play over shots with no condensation cloud (the cloud only appears in the 0 to 4 s opener). No danger and a weak resolution; 21-06 tells the stronger Saturn V story.
Footage is a CG animation made before the test, presented as the real flight. Dropped.
Clean, well-cropped 16mm launch footage, but it is the fourth Artemis II liftoff angle in the queue and shows a routine launch with no visible danger.

r3 removed the animation opener and the interview cut-ins, but the real footage is hazy and distant: the liftoff is a speck for 8 seconds and the in-air capsule shots are pale and repetitive. No visible danger at Short scale, and a pad abort already ran as ccf-20261121-16.
Third F/A-18 incentive ride in this batch with the same hook pattern, and the weakest one: the opener is a calm back-seat shot with sky and no visible maneuver. Interchangeable with -05 and -06.

No danger or close call: a photographer's T-38 ride, mostly cockpit selfies and a ladder shot after the opening formation, and nothing on screen backs the 'landed with every camera still rolling' outcome.
Calm record flight with no danger on screen; about ten seconds on the same altimeter dial, and it is the third X-15 Short from the same documentary in this batch.
Calm blue-sky basket transfer with no visible danger; most of the 30 s is the same underside shot of the Jayhawk from a rain-spotted lens, and the 33 s source has nothing else to cut to. Dropped.
About 35 seconds of grey lunar surface through the LM window with nothing changing; the computer alarms are only narrated, never seen, and the last shot is a letterboxed quarantine room.
One continuous helicopter shot of a normal, uneventful launch for the whole Short; no danger, no turn, and the rocket is small in the frame.
